Risk title: Contract renewals fail to deliver planned rate uplift
Cause: OUTCOME DRIVERS (market): tender pressure, soft utilization, customer resistance to re-pricing toward newbuild parity. TRIDENT-SIDE FAILURE MODES (actionable): (1) renewal calendar without per-contract rate/terms mandate; (2) weak comps / newbuild-parity pack for negotiators; (3) no BATNA (redeploy/idle/other region) so we accept soft rates; (4) late escalation when renewal forecast slips vs uplift plan; (5) incentives biased to volume over rate quality; (6) indexation and term playbook not applied in negotiation.
Risk event: Material renewals close at rates below the organic rate-uplift plan.
Consequences: Like-for-like EBITDA and cash generation undershoot the value-creation plan.
Current mitigation: S&BD+Commercial: (1) 12–24 month renewal calendar with target TC rate, indexation, and duration per contract; (2) pre-negotiation brief (comps, customer alternatives, BATNA) signed before talks open; (3) formal rate/terms mandate from CCO/S&BD; (4) monthly renewal gap vs plan with escalation if below corridor; (5) deal review gate before signing below corridor; (6) link SBD-P05 operating agenda to each material renewal.
Evidence / rationale: Operationalized for S&BD: outcome risk broken into Trident controllable failure modes and mitigations — validate with Commercial.

Risk title: Fleet redeployment misses higher-return regional demand
Cause: OUTCOME DRIVERS: regional willingness-to-pay and demand differ; tonnage can remain in lower-return regions while another region (e.g. Chile) is short. TRIDENT-SIDE FAILURE MODES (redeployment is NOT liquid): (1) market intel not turned into a timed portfolio case (demand evidence, vessel fit, constraints); (2) treating inter-region moves as a simple shuffle — ignoring reconstruction, yard slot, transit, flag/class/biosecurity, and commercial exit costs; (3) no ranked options with full economics (move / wait / serve another way); (4) slow decision rights between S&BD, Commercial, and Ops so the Chile window closes; (5) contract/exit constraints in the weak region not mapped early; (6) no trigger when regional EBITDA or rate-utilization spread vs plan exceeds threshold — so no case is opened; (7) Chile (or destination) cannibalisation ignored: stronger incoming vessel can idle or reprice less competitive tonnage already in region.
Risk event: Vessels remain under-monetized relative to achievable regional rate and utilization differentials.
Consequences: Organic EBITDA growth lags peers and the platform's global flexibility advantage is underused.
Current mitigation: S&BD-led portfolio case (not a liquid move): (1) quarterly regional rate/utilization/EBITDA heat map vs P05 plan; (2) when spread vs plan breaches agreed threshold, open a redeployment case with owner and decision deadline (do not auto-move); (3) ranked shortlist with vessel fit PLUS reconstruction scope/cost/time, transit and regulatory path, and exit/novation costs in the weak region; (4) destination impact pack: expected cannibalisation on existing Chile (or other) vessels — utilisation, rate, residual value; (5) decision forum S&BD-Commercial-Ops: approve move / wait / alternative only if net fleet EBITDA after transaction costs and cannibalisation clears the hurdle (SBD-P02/P05/P06); (6) document rejected moves so the threshold does not keep reopening the same weak case.
Evidence / rationale: Operationalized: focus on decision speed and intel-to-action, not only market geography — validate.

Risk title: Crewing and operating-cost inflation outpaces rate growth
Cause: OUTCOME DRIVERS: wage/opex inflation vs renewal revenue. TRIDENT-SIDE FAILURE MODES: (1) rate mandates ignore cost inflation outlook; (2) no joint rate-vs-cost bridge in renewals; (3) CPI/pass-through terms not pushed when cost outlook is hot; (4) S&BD does not force Commercial+Crewing+Ops cost view into pricing; (5) lag between cost signals and renewal instructions.
Risk event: Contribution margins on the existing fleet compress despite stable utilization.
Consequences: Organic EBITDA and cash conversion fall short of budget even when commercial volumes hold.
Current mitigation: S&BD coordinates: (1) quarterly cost-inflation outlook from Crewing/Ops/Finance into pricing corridor; (2) renewal mandates include minimum indexation/pass-through when cost outlook exceeds X%; (3) rate-vs-cost bridge required in pre-negotiation brief; (4) reject/escalate renewals that lock flat rates into a rising-cost window; (5) track margin after crewing/opex, not only headline TC (SBD-P05/P12).
Evidence / rationale: Operationalized: S&BD lever is pricing/terms discipline fed by cost intel — Ops/Crewing own cost delivery.
